shlokas.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा किम्पुरुषोत्पत्तिं लक्ष्मणो भरतस्तदा । आश्चर्यमिति चाब्रूतामुभौ रामं जनेश्वरम् ।। 7.89.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śrutvā kimpuruṣotpattiṃ lakṣmaṇo bharatastadā | āścaryamiti cābrūtāmubhau rāmaṃ janeśvaram || 7.89.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard the account of the origin of the Kimpurushas, Lakshmana and Bharata then both said to Rama, the lord of men, "How wonderful!"

shlokas.sanskrit: अथ रामः कथामेतां भूय एव महायशाः । कथयामास धर्मात्मा प्रजापतिसुतस्य वै ।। 7.89.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: atha rāmaḥ kathāmetāṃ bhūya eva mahāyaśāḥ | kathayāmāsa dharmātmā prajāpatisutasya vai || 7.89.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the illustrious and righteous-souled Rama once again recounted this story of the son of Prajapati.

shlokas.sanskrit: सर्वास्ता विद्रुता दृष्ट्वा किन्नरीर्ऋषिसत्तमः । उवाच रूपसम्पन्नां तां स्त्रियं प्रहसन्निव ।। 7.89.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sarvāstā vidrutā dṛṣṭvā kinnarīrṛṣisattamaḥ | uvāca rūpasampannāṃ tāṃ striyaṃ prahasanniva || 7.89.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Seeing all those Kinnari women flee away, that foremost of sages spoke, as if laughing, to the one beautiful woman among them.

shlokas.sanskrit: सोमस्याहं सुदयितः सुतः सुरुचिरानने । भजस्व मां वरारोहे भक्त्या स्निग्धेन चक्षुषा ।। 7.89.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: somasyāhaṃ sudayitaḥ sutaḥ surucirānane | bhajasva māṃ varārohe bhaktyā snigdhena cakṣuṣā || 7.89.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "O fair-faced one, I am the dearly beloved son of Soma. Love me, O lovely-hipped lady, with devotion and with a tender eye."

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा शून्ये स्वजनवर्जिते । इला सुरुचिरप्रख्यं प्रत्युवाच महाग्रहम् ।। 7.89.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā śūnye svajanavarjite | ilā suruciraprakhyaṃ pratyuvāca mahāgraham || 7.89.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard that speech of his in that lonely spot devoid of her own people, Ila answered the great planet whose radiance resembled the lovely moon.

shlokas.sanskrit: अहं कामचरी सौम्य तवास्मि वशवर्तिनी । प्रशाधि मां सोमसुत यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ।। 7.89.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ahaṃ kāmacarī saumya tavāsmi vaśavartinī | praśādhi māṃ somasuta yathecchasi tathā kuru || 7.89.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "O gentle one, I move at will, and I am subject to your wishes. Command me, O son of Soma; do with me as you desire."

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्यास्तदद्भुतप्रख्यं श्रुत्वा हर्षमुपागतः । स वै कामी सह तया रेमे चन्द्रमसः सुतः ।। 7.89.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasyāstadadbhutaprakhyaṃ śrutvā harṣamupāgataḥ | sa vai kāmī saha tayā reme candramasaḥ sutaḥ || 7.89.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing that wondrous-seeming reply of hers, the son of the Moon was overcome with joy, and being amorous, he sported together with her.

shlokas.sanskrit: बुधस्य माधवो मासस्तामिलां रुचिराननाम् । गतो रमयतो ऽत्यर्थं क्षणवत्तस्य कामिनः ।। 7.89.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: budhasya mādhavo māsastāmilāṃ rucirānanām | gato ramayato 'tyarthaṃ kṣaṇavattasya kāminaḥ || 7.89.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: The spring month of Madhava passed for Budha, as he took exceeding delight with that lovely-faced Ila, like a single moment for that lover.

shlokas.sanskrit: अथ मासे तु सम्पूर्णे पूर्णेन्दुसदृशाननः । प्रजापतिसुतः श्रीमाञ्छयने प्रत्यबुध्यत ।। 7.89.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: atha māse tu sampūrṇe pūrṇendusadṛśānanaḥ | prajāpatisutaḥ śrīmāñchayane pratyabudhyata || 7.89.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then, when the month was complete, the glorious son of Prajapati, whose face resembled the full moon, awoke upon his couch.

shlokas.sanskrit: सो ऽपश्यत्सोमजं तत्र तपन्तं सलिलाशये । ऊर्ध्वबाहुं निरालम्बं तं राजा प्रत्यभाषत ।। 7.89.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: so 'paśyatsomajaṃ tatra tapantaṃ salilāśaye | ūrdhvabāhuṃ nirālambaṃ taṃ rājā pratyabhāṣata || 7.89.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: He saw there the son of Soma practicing austerity in a body of water, his arms raised aloft and unsupported; and the king addressed him.

shlokas.sanskrit: भगवन्पर्वतं दुर्गं प्रविष्टो ऽस्मि सहानुगः । न च पश्यामि तत्सैन्यं क्व नु ते मामका गताः ।। 7.89.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bhagavanparvataṃ durgaṃ praviṣṭo 'smi sahānugaḥ | na ca paśyāmi tatsainyaṃ kva nu te māmakā gatāḥ || 7.89.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "O blessed one, I entered this rugged mountain together with my followers, yet I do not see that army of mine. Where indeed have my men gone?"

shlokas.sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा तस्य राजर्षेर्नष्टसञ्ज्ञस्य भाषितम् । प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं सान्त्वयन्परया गिरा ।। 7.89.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tacchrutvā tasya rājarṣernaṣṭasañjñasya bhāṣitam | pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ sāntvayanparayā girā || 7.89.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing that speech of the royal sage, who had lost his memory, Budha replied with auspicious words, soothing him with surpassing speech.

shlokas.sanskrit: अश्मवर्षेण महता भृत्यास्ते विनिपातिताः । त्वं चाश्रमपदे सुप्तो वातवर्षभयार्दितः ।। 7.89.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: aśmavarṣeṇa mahatā bhṛtyāste vinipātitāḥ | tvaṃ cāśramapade supto vātavarṣabhayārditaḥ || 7.89.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Your servants were struck down by a great rain of stones, and you, tormented by fear of the wind and rain, lay asleep in this hermitage."

shlokas.sanskrit: समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते निर्भयो विगतज्वरः । फलमूलाशनो वीर निवसेह यथासुखम् ।। 7.89.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: samāśvasihi bhadraṃ te nirbhayo vigatajvaraḥ | phalamūlāśano vīra nivaseha yathāsukham || 7.89.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Take comfort; may it be well with you. Free from fear and rid of distress, O hero, dwell here at your ease, living on fruits and roots."

shlokas.sanskrit: स राजा तेन वाक्येन प्रत्याश्वस्तो महामतिः । प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं दीनो भृत्यक्षयाद् भृशम् ।। 7.89.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa rājā tena vākyena pratyāśvasto mahāmatiḥ | pratyuvāca tato vākyaṃ dīno bhṛtyakṣayād bhṛśam || 7.89.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Reassured by those words, the king of great intellect, yet sorely grieved at the destruction of his servants, then spoke these words.

shlokas.sanskrit: त्यक्ष्याम्यहं स्वकं राज्यं नाहं भृत्यैर्विनाकृतः । वर्तयेयं क्षणं ब्रह्मन्समनुज्ञातुमर्हसि ।। 7.89.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tyakṣyāmyahaṃ svakaṃ rājyaṃ nāhaṃ bhṛtyairvinākṛtaḥ | vartayeyaṃ kṣaṇaṃ brahmansamanujñātumarhasi || 7.89.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "I shall renounce my own kingdom; I will not live deprived of my servants. I would tarry but a moment, O brahmin; you should grant me leave."

shlokas.sanskrit: सुतो धर्मपरो ब्रह्मञ्ज्येष्ठो मम महायशाः । शशबिन्दुरिति ख्यातः स मे राज्यं प्रपत्स्यते ।। 7.89.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: suto dharmaparo brahmañjyeṣṭho mama mahāyaśāḥ | śaśabinduriti khyātaḥ sa me rājyaṃ prapatsyate || 7.89.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "I have an eldest son, O brahmin, devoted to dharma and of great fame, renowned by the name Shashabindu; he shall inherit my kingdom."

shlokas.sanskrit: न हि शक्ष्याम्यहं हित्वा भृत्यदारान्सुखान्वितान् । प्रतिवक्तुं महातेजः किञ्चिदप्यशुभं वचः ।। 7.89.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: na hi śakṣyāmyahaṃ hitvā bhṛtyadārānsukhānvitān | prativaktuṃ mahātejaḥ kiñcidapyaśubhaṃ vacaḥ || 7.89.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "For I shall not be able, O greatly resplendent one, having forsaken my servants and my comfort-blessed wives, to utter even a single ill-omened word."

shlokas.sanskrit: तथा ब्रुवति राजेन्द्रे बुधः परममद्भुतम् । सान्त्वपूर्वमथोवाच वासस्त इह रोचताम् ।। 7.89.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tathā bruvati rājendre budhaḥ paramamadbhutam | sāntvapūrvamathovāca vāsasta iha rocatām || 7.89.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When the lord of kings spoke thus, Budha, exceedingly amazed, then said with conciliating words, "Let your dwelling here be pleasing to you."

shlokas.sanskrit: न सन्तापस्त्वया कार्यः कार्दमेय महाबल । संवत्सरोषितस्येह कारयिष्यामि ते हितम् ।। 7.89.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: na santāpastvayā kāryaḥ kārdameya mahābala | saṃvatsaroṣitasyeha kārayiṣyāmi te hitam || 7.89.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "You should feel no grief, O mighty son of Kardama. When you have dwelt here a year, I shall bring about your welfare."

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा बुधस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः । वासाय विदधे बुद्धिं यदुक्तं ब्रह्मवादिना ।। 7.89.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā budhasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ | vāsāya vidadhe buddhiṃ yaduktaṃ brahmavādinā || 7.89.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard those words of Budha of untiring deeds, Ila resolved to dwell there, just as had been counselled by that expounder of the sacred Veda.

shlokas.sanskrit: मासं स स्त्री तदा भूत्वा रमयत्यनिशं शुदा । मासं पुरुषभावेन धर्मबुद्धिं चकार सः ।। 7.89.22 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: māsaṃ sa strī tadā bhūtvā ramayatyaniśaṃ śudā | māsaṃ puruṣabhāvena dharmabuddhiṃ cakāra saḥ || 7.89.22 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: For one month, becoming a woman then, she sported ceaselessly with delight; and for the next month, with the nature of a man restored, he turned his mind to righteousness.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः सा नवमे मासि इला सोमसुतात्सुतम् । जनयामास सुश्रोणी पुरूरवसमूर्जितम् ।। 7.89.23 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tataḥ sā navame māsi ilā somasutātsutam | janayāmāsa suśroṇī purūravasamūrjitam || 7.89.23 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then in the ninth month that fair-hipped woman Ila gave birth, by Budha the son of Soma, to a mighty son, the powerful Pururavas.

shlokas.sanskrit: जातमात्रं तु सुश्रोणी पितुर्हस्ते न्यवेशयत् । बुधस्य समवर्णभमिला पुत्रं महाबलम् ।। 7.89.24 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: jātamātraṃ tu suśroṇī piturhaste nyaveśayat | budhasya samavarṇabhamilā putraṃ mahābalam || 7.89.24 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: As soon as he was born, the fair-hipped Ila placed in the hands of his father Budha the mighty son, who was of a complexion like Budha's own.

shlokas.sanskrit: बुधस्तु पुरुषीभूतं स वै संवत्सरान्तरम् । कथाभी रमयामास धर्मयुक्ताभिरात्मवान् ।। 7.89.25 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: budhastu puruṣībhūtaṃ sa vai saṃvatsarāntaram | kathābhī ramayāmāsa dharmayuktābhirātmavān || 7.89.25 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And the self-possessed Budha, when that one had become a man again, delighted him for the space of a year with discourses imbued with righteousness.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोननवतितमः सर्गः ।। 89 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe ekonanavatitamaḥ sargaḥ || 89 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus ends the eighty-ninth canto in the venerable Uttara Kanda of the sacred Ramayana, the first epic poem composed by the sage Valmiki.
